title: Week 2 sync - infra creds, traffic shaping and perf plan
summary: Weekly POC check-in focusing on access handoff, infra readiness (VPC peering, KMS), preliminary perf anomalies on 2k token context, and plan for traffic shaping and benchmark run later this week. Agreement to exchange short checklist and run a scoped perf test Friday with canary traffic.
topics: next steps: perf run and security docs
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check — can we do a quick round of who is on the line?
[00:06] Rajesh: Rajesh here, I'm leading the ML side for the POC.
[00:09] Elena: Elena, platform engineering. We own the cluster and networking.
[00:12] Mike: Mike from security. I'll be looking at KMS and audit logs.
[00:16] Daniel: Daniel from Redwood SE. I'll be running the bench and helping with tuning.
[00:20] Sofia: Great. Quick agenda: access handoff, infra readiness (VPC peering/egress), perf observations from the smoke tests you ran yesterday, and plan for the Friday benchmark. Any additions?
[00:31] Elena: No additions. We want to confirm SSO/SCIM later but today focus on network and creds.
[00:36] Sofia: Perfect. Elena, status on the access tickets?
[00:40] Elena: We created the VPC peering request but we hit a routing table flub — some subnets weren't propagated. So peering is pending until we update the route propagation. Also, we only opened 443 outbound to Redwood, but we need to allow 1024-65535 for the ephemeral data flows? I might be misremembering, the doc said ports for data plane.
[00:58] Daniel: Right, the dataplane uses ephemeral high ports for chunked streaming; 443 for the control plane and 10k+ ephemeral for the actual streaming grpc. We did put that in the infra checklist we shared.
[01:10] Elena: Ok we'll add that. Rajesh: on the ML side we saw something odd in yesterday's smoke — the 2k token calls had spikes up to ~820ms p95 then sometimes to 1.2s, whereas 512 token tests were stable around 160ms p95. Any known causes?
[01:30] Daniel: A couple likely things: 1) KV cache heat — if the model isn't warmed and cache misses occur, you get extra decodes on prefix. 2) batching config might be set to conservative so small bursts are hitting inference cold. 3) we saw occasional kernel scheduling jitter on the GPU in the dedicated node — though this should be rare.
[01:50] Mike: On the security front, we need to confirm the default logs retention and whether Redwood can push audit logs to our SIEM. Also KMS — does Redwood support customer-managed keys in this pilot?
[02:03] Sofia: For pilots on hosted we can provide a temporary encrypted key; customer-managed KMS/HSM is supported in Private/Dedicated modes. For the POC we can enable an integration pattern where you push logs to S3 and we provide an export script, or if you prefer we can set up direct forwarder to Splunk via HTTPS. We'll send the security playbook.
[02:22] Mike: Ok please send the playbook and the minimal compliance attestation; we need SOC2 type references.
[02:28] Sofia: Yep, noted.
[02:30] Daniel: Back to latency — can I ask what batch size and max tokens were configured in your smoke harness?
[02:36] Rajesh: We used batch_size 8, max_new_tokens 2000, and a request_rate of ~4 requests/sec. Clients are a mix of long form summarization and live assistant calls.
[02:46] Daniel: 4 rps with batch 8 and 2k tokens will create some tail risk. For the Friday bench we want to test a few knobs: continuous batching with warm prefixes, KV cache enabled, and also try quantized model variant if you can accept some quality tradeoff.
[03:01] Elena: How disruptive is turning on continuous batching? Our infra team worries about waiting latency.
[03:06] Daniel: Continuous batching pools inflight requests up to a microsecond target. It slightly increases median latency for single-request bursts but greatly reduces p95 in steady-state. We'll show tradeoffs in the bench with curves.
[03:18] Sofia: For the Friday run we propose two profiles: 1) latency-prioritized (small batch, aggressive cold-start warming) and 2) cost/throughput-prioritized (larger batch, quantized model). We'll measure p50/p95/p99 and per-token cost estimate.
[03:33] Rajesh: Sounds good. Also we saw a couple of errors in the smoke — 502 timeouts when context exceeded 3k tokens in one case. Is there a hard limit?
[03:41] Daniel: No hard limit at 3k for the model, but in your current config there might be request size caps on the loadbalancer or a proxy that drops long streaming connections. We should check LB timeout and max header/body sizes.
[03:53] Elena: Noted — we'll surface the proxy config.
[03:56] Mike: About auditability — can we get token-level usage maps for the pilot? We need to correlate inputs/outputs with logs without leaking PII.
[04:05] Sofia: We can provide aggregated token-level usage plus request IDs for correlation; for raw payloads we'd need explicit agreement on retention and redaction. We'll include the retention options in the security doc.
[04:18] Daniel: Quick note on routing — if capacity is constrained we can route low-risk demo traffic to a smaller cheaper model. For your use-case (medical summarization), we recommend fallback only for non-PHI flows.
[04:31] Rajesh: Understood. Also timeline: we want to have the perf run Friday and then a short executive touchpoint Monday to decide rollout. Is that still realistic?
[04:40] Sofia: Yes. Friday perf run, results by EOD Friday, Monday exec ~30m.
[04:46] Elena: Ok. Any blockers on our side?
[04:49] Daniel: Two small ones: 1) we need an SSH bastion key to access the log bundle (read-only) and 2) confirm the VPC peering route propagation fix.
[04:59] Elena: I'll open the ticket to add propagation and allow the ephemeral port range. SSH key — we prefer to use our internal secrets store, can you accept a signed cert instead of a static key?
[05:09] Sofia: We can accept signed certs; we have a pattern for that. We'll share the instructions.
[05:15] Mike: Also, security wants to see proof of encryption-in-transit end-to-end, specifically TLS versions and cipher suites.
[05:23] Daniel: We use TLS1.3 by default on the control plane and mutual TLS for certain data-plane flows. We'll include cipher suites in the playbook.
[05:32] Rajesh: Regarding quality, if we try the quantized model variant what's the expected delta on ROUGE/BLEU (rough guess)?
[05:40] Daniel: Usually 0-3% relative degradation on long-form summarization; depends on prompt engineering. We'll include a recommended evaluation prompt set so you can compare.
[05:51] Elena: Anything else?
[05:53] Sofia: Quick recap of tangible next steps and owners, then we'll wrap.
[06:00] Daniel: I'll run a debug bench on Friday morning at 0900 PT and then full run at 1300 PT. Need the VPC fix and the SSH/signed cert by 0800 PT.
[06:12] Elena: We'll push the routing table change tonight and confirm by email.
[06:16] Mike: Security will review the playbook when you send it; target response by Monday.
[06:21] Sofia: I'll send the security playbook, the infra checklist, and a temporary API key for smoke tests. Also sending the Splunk forwarding guide.
[06:30] Rajesh: Great, thanks. Looking forward to the Friday run.
[06:33] Sofia: Ok everyone, thanks for the time. We'll follow up in Slack and email with the materials.
[06:38] [END]

Redwood SE: run Friday benchmark (debug at 09:00 PT, full run 13:00 PT) and send results by 2025-02-21 EOD
Schedule 30m exec touchpoint Monday 2025-02-24 to review results
